listingTitle: Keep behavior with the data it uses
title: Keep behavior with the data it uses
why: A method dominated by one parameter’s members may own misplaced behavior.
suggestion: Consider moving the behavior to the foreign type or its API.
limitations: Requires five accesses across three members and sixty percent of received accesses; Dart direct and null-aware accesses contribute to that denominator, while parameters matching the enclosing class type, AST visitor implementations, object-literal projection methods, and accesses solely composing a returned Flutter Widget are excluded.
Findings identify each method declaration rather than the enclosing class header, so same-named overloads retain distinct source locations.

The shared analyzer excludes Java methods whose entire body returns a completed Type.builder()/newBuilder() projection and whose argument calls are only parameter-rooted, zero-argument get/is/has accessor chains. Additional statements, other argument calls, mutation or callback syntax, unfinished builders, and getAnd/getOr operations remain eligible. Getter naming is conventional evidence, not resolved proof of side-effect freedom.
Comments, strings, generated, test, example, and vendored sources follow normal analysis classification and suppression controls.
